Main article: [Climate change in Asia](/wiki/Climate_change_in_Asia "Climate change in Asia")

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/28/Guo_2023_Asia_IVT_projections.jpg/250px-Guo_2023_Asia_IVT_projections.jpg)](/wiki/File:Guo_2023_Asia_IVT_projections.jpg)

Greater warming increases the amount of moisture in the atmosphere over Asia, which directly leads to extreme precipitation. Probability of 20-year, 50-year and 100-year extremes consistently increases with warming across Asia. In the most affected parts of South Asia, up to a 15-fold average increase for 100-year extremes is possible under 3 °C (5.4 °F) of warming.[[202]](#cite_note-Guo2023-209)

South Asian countries are expected to experience more flooding in the future as the monsoon pattern intensifies.[[203]](#cite_note-AR6_WGII_Chapter10-210): 1459 Across Asia as a whole, 100-year extremes in vapour transport (directly related to extreme precipitation) would become 2.6 times more frequent under 1.5 °C (2.7 °F) of global warming, yet 3.9 and 7.5 times more frequent under 2 °C (3.6 °F) and 3 °C (5.4 °F). In parts of South Asia, they could become up to 15 times more frequent.[[202]](#cite_note-Guo2023-209) At the same time, up to two-thirds of glacier ice in the Hindu Kush region may melt by 2100 under high warming, and these glaciers feed the water basin of over 220 million people.[[203]](#cite_note-AR6_WGII_Chapter10-210): 1487 As glacier meltwater flow diminishes after 2050, [Hydropower](/wiki/Hydropower "Hydropower") generation would become less predictable and reliable, while agriculture would become more reliant on the intensified monsoon than ever before.[[204]](#cite_note-:HKH2019Climate-211)[[205]](#cite_note-:HKH2019Cryo-212)[[206]](#cite_note-:HKH2019Water-213) Around 2050, people living in the [Ganges](/wiki/Ganges "Ganges") and [Indus](/wiki/Indus "Indus") river basins (where up to 60% of non-monsoon irrigation co

**Rosario**,[[a]](#cite_note-5) officially the **Autonomous City of Rosario**,[[b]](#cite_note-6)[[5]](#cite_note-ellit-7)[[6]](#cite_note-ros3-8)[[7]](#cite_note-cons-9) is a city in central [Argentina](/wiki/Argentina "Argentina"), in the south of the [province](/wiki/Provinces_of_Argentina "Provinces of Argentina") of [Santa Fe](/wiki/Santa_Fe_Province "Santa Fe Province"). Located 300 km (186 mi) northwest of [Buenos Aires](/wiki/Buenos_Aires "Buenos Aires") on the west bank of the [Paraná River](/wiki/Paran%C3%A1_River "Paraná River"), it is the country's third-most populous city after Buenos Aires and [Córdoba](/wiki/C%C3%B3rdoba,_Argentina "Córdoba, Argentina"). With a growing and important [metropolitan area](/wiki/Metropolitan_area "Metropolitan area"), [Greater Rosario](/wiki/Greater_Rosario "Greater Rosario") has an estimated population of 1,750,000 as of 2020.[[8]](#cite_note-10)[[9]](#cite_note-eph-11) One of its main attractions includes the [neoclassical](/wiki/Neoclassical_architecture "Neoclassical architecture"), [Art Nouveau](/wiki/Art_Nouveau "Art Nouveau"),[[10]](#cite_note-12) and [Art Deco](/wiki/Art_Deco "Art Deco") architecture that has been preserved in hundreds of residences, houses and public buildings. The city is also famous for being the birthplace of Argentine footballer [Lionel Messi](/wiki/Lionel_Messi "Lionel Messi").[[11]](#cite_note-13)

Rosario is the head city of the [Rosario Department](/wiki/Rosario_Department "Rosario Department") and is located at the heart of the major industrial corridor in Argentina. The city is a major [railroad](/wiki/Rail_transport "Rail transport") terminal and the shipping center for north-eastern Argentina. Ships reach the city via the Paraná River, which allows the existence of a 10-metre-deep (34 ft) [port](/wiki/Port "Port"). [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/09/Rigaud_Hyacinthe_-_Louis_XIV%2C_roi_de_France.jpg/250px-Rigaud_Hyacinthe_-_Louis_XIV%2C_roi_de_France.jpg)](/wiki/File:Rigaud_Hyacinthe_-_Louis_XIV,_roi_de_France.jpg)

Louis in 1701

On his deathbed in 1700, Charles II of Spain unexpectedly changed his will. The clear demonstration of French military superiority for many decades before this time, the pro-French faction at the court of Spain, and even [Pope Innocent XII](/wiki/Pope_Innocent_XII "Pope Innocent XII") convinced him that France was more likely to preserve his empire intact. He thus offered the entire empire to the Dauphin's second son Philip, Duke of Anjou, provided it remained undivided. Anjou was not in the direct line of French succession, thus his accession would not cause a Franco-Spanish union.[[91]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTELynn1999268-93) If Anjou refused, the throne would be offered to his younger brother [Charles, Duke of Berry](/wiki/Charles,_Duke_of_Berry_(1686%E2%80%931714) "Charles, Duke of Berry (1686–1714)"). If the Duke of Berry declined it, it would go to Archduke Charles, then to the distantly related [House of Savoy](/wiki/House_of_Savoy "House of Savoy") if Charles declined it.[[92]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEKamen20016-94)

Louis was confronted with a difficult choice. He could agree to a partition of the Spanish possessions and avoid a general war, or accept Charles II's will and alienate much of Europe. He may initially have been inclined to abide by the partition treaties, but the Dauphin's insistence persuaded him otherwise.[[93]](#cite_note-FOOTNOTEDunlop2000358-95) Moreover, Louis's foreign minister, [Jean-Baptiste Colbert, marquis de Torcy](/wiki/Jean-Baptiste_Colbert,_marquis_de_Torcy "Jean-Baptiste Colbert, marquis de Torcy"), pointed out that war with the Emperor would almost certainly ensue whether Louis accepted th

The **Academy Award for Best Director** (officially known as the **Academy Award of Merit for Directing**) is an award presented annually by the [Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences](/wiki/Academy_of_Motion_Picture_Arts_and_Sciences "Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences") (AMPAS). AlphaGo logo

AlphaGo is a computer program developed by [Google DeepMind](/wiki/Google_DeepMind "Google DeepMind") to play the board game [Go](/wiki/Go_(game) "Go (game)"). AlphaGo's algorithm uses a combination of [machine learning](/wiki/Machine_learning "Machine learning") and [tree search](/wiki/Tree_search "Tree search") techniques, combined with extensive training, both from human and computer play. The system's neural networks were initially bootstrapped from human game-play expertise. AlphaGo was initially trained to mimic human play by attempting to match the moves of expert players from recorded historical games, using a [KGS Go Server](/wiki/KGS_Go_Server "KGS Go Server") database of around 30 million moves from 160,000 games by KGS 6 to 9 dan human players.[[13]](#cite_note-AlphaGo-13)[[28]](#cite_note-MetzWired2016-28) Once it had reached a certain degree of proficiency, it was trained further by being set to play large numbers of games against other instances of itself, using [reinforcement learning](/wiki/Reinforcement_learning "Reinforcement learning") to improve its play.[[29]](#cite_note-googlego-29) The system does not use a "database" of moves to play. As one of the creators of AlphaGo explained:[[30]](#cite_note-wired.com-30)

> Although we have programmed this machine to play, we have no idea what moves it will come up with. Its moves are an [emergent](/wiki/Emergence "Emergence") phenomenon from the training. We just create the data sets and the training algorithms. But the moves it then comes up with are out of our hands—and much better than we, as Go players, could come up with.

Officially formed with ExxonMobil's 2022 corporate restructuring, and currently led by former [General Motors](/wiki/General_Motors "General Motors") president [Dan Ammann](/wiki/Dan_Ammann "Dan Ammann"), Low Carbon Solutions is the company's alternative energy division. Low Carbon Solutions conducts research on clean energy technologies, including [algae biofuels](/wiki/Algae_fuel "Algae fuel"), [biodiesel](/wiki/Biodiesel "Biodiesel") made from agricultural waste, carbonate [fuel cells](/wiki/Fuel_cell "Fuel cell"), and refining crude oil into plastic by using a [membrane](/wiki/Membrane "Membrane") and [osmosis](/wiki/Osmosis "Osmosis") instead of heat.[[56]](#cite_note-bloomberg031117-57)[[57]](#cite_note-58) Exxon's work on low-carbon energy projects is a fraction of the $1 billion a year Exxon spends on general research and the $8 billion it has spent since 2000.[[58]](#cite_note-59)

As of 2023, the company was in the process of designing its inaugural large-scale plant dedicated to producing low-carbon hydrogen, situated within its refining and petrochemical complex in [Baytown, Texas](/wiki/Baytown,_Texas "Baytown, Texas"). This project is set to become the world's largest low-carbon hydrogen project.[[59]](#cite_note-60)

Demographic history of New York City :: Overview :: chunk_0001
See also: [Race and ethnicity in New York City](/wiki/Race_and_ethnicity_in_New_York_City "Race and ethnicity in New York City")

The population of [New York City](/wiki/New_York_City "New York City") was over 90% [Non-Hispanic White](/wiki/Non-Hispanic_Whites "Non-Hispanic Whites") until the post-World War II era.[[1]](#cite_note-nycrace-1) Large numbers of Blacks, Hispanics, or Asians began settling in [Manhattan](/wiki/Manhattan "Manhattan") in the 1920s and in the rest of NYC after [World War II](/wiki/World_War_II "World War II").[[1]](#cite_note-nycrace-1) The slowest area in the city to change its racial makeup was [Staten Island](/wiki/Staten_Island "Staten Island"), which was the only borough of New York City to retain a Non-Hispanic White majority after the 1980s.[[1]](#cite_note-nycrace-1) Between 1900 and 2010, New York City's total Black population increased by about thirty-five times, while its Asian population increased by over one-hundred-and-fifty times over the same period.[[1]](#cite_note-nycrace-1) The large [Black migration](/wiki/Great_Migration_(African_American) "Great Migration (African American)") to New York City helped form the [Harlem Renaissance](/wiki/Harlem_Renaissance "Harlem Renaissance"), a rich cultural period for the African Americans living in New York (especially in [Harlem](/wiki/Harlem "Harlem") neighborhood, the namesake) between the end of World War I and the Great Depression. New York's Hispanic population increased by almost twenty times between 1940 and 2010, while its total Non-Hispanic White population decreased by over 60% over the same time period.[[1]](#cite_note-nycrace-1)
